reviewedItems.requestedAction: Document status states, setup blockers, retry actions, technical evidence, and user-safe message rules.
reviewedItems.rationale: OPEN_CONTENT_GAP: the unchanged Axis article describes a global all-required-publications barrier and undifferentiated INITIALIZE recovery. Current BackOffice additionally accepts one afterPublicationStepCode under signed operatorEnterpriseCode authority, can execute that operator's selected DATA_RELEASE once its own publications are CURRENT while foreign stages remain pending, and returns selectionRequired/selectableStepCodes/AUTHORITY_PENDING plus exact-plan observations. The guide does not explain this selection, authority or recovery contract and its unconditional global barrier is inaccurate for scoped profiles. Existing status/message explanations do not satisfy the complete requested setup-blocker and retry explanation.
sourceFindings: afterPublicationSelection/isPreparationOperator bind one configured stage to the original signed human access token, tenant and enterprise aliases. assertInitiationScope restricts narrow Commerce groups to that operator stage; the POST initiate route now accepts afterPublicationStepCode.

scopedAfterPublicationPreparation checks operatorPublicationsReady for the current operator, executes at most the selected DATA_RELEASE and refreshes status. Foreign stages can remain AUTHORITY_PENDING or use aggregate-only exact-plan observations. This contradicts the guide's unconditional global publication barrier for scoped profiles.

setupObservation uses the deployment token on fixed /publications/setup/observe and verifies plan/checksum/stage/profile/baseline/tenant/enterprise/runtime identity; SOURCE/TARGET/SOURCE checks reject changed evidence. Read observation grants neither selection nor foreign mutation.

reviewedItems.item: Commerce product, price, inventory, and fulfillment authoring
reviewedItems.requestedAction: Document data dependencies, creation lanes, publication, search projection, fulfillment evidence, and browser proof.
reviewedItems.rationale: Re-read the five canonical Commerce authoring/Promotion/Digital/Fulfillment articles against changed Pricing, Digital merchant, Digital ownership and Promotion lifecycle sources and the ownership contract. Retained publication remains separate from operational stock; original merchant receipts and exact ownership readback remain required. Unselected ownership availability is bounded unavailable supply, selected faults still refuse, and lifecycle CAS preserves original encrypted issuance. Current articles accurately retain private confirmation, original-sale refund, exact millisecond identity, simulated/unverified ITEM labels, unavailable real ITEM delivery and disabled used-benefit inverse limits. No financial, native or provider qualification follows.
sourceFindings: Pricing prepareSetup/createGoverned/validateSetup retain exact source capture and shared nPublish authority. authorizeTarget rereads stored intent; legacyCasRecovery requires exact operation/scope/root/source and reason/approver/reference, refuses competing history and does not activate from caller approval flags.

Digital confirmation retains original staff/outlet revision, receipt/key and pricedBinding, protected receipt readback before redeem and exact completed-receipt replay. MERCHANT_RECEIPT deliveredAt is a Date for original marker.confirmedAt; it remains workflow coordination, not physical delivery, as the current article explains.

Digital ownership timestamp/verifyRecord compare Date and ISO instants with milliseconds, require one exact current owner row and verify entitlement/delivery after save. The canonical refund section explicitly rejects lossy coercion and one-millisecond drift.

Ownership availability returns bounded unavailable supply only when unselected/unqualified. Selected integration configuration, retained pins and owner evidence still refuse faults; reserve/write/refund remain strict. The current non-data contract describes this without allocation or financial qualification.

Promotion commitLifecycleCoupon rejects changed/cleared protectedToken/secureIssuance/secureIssuanceCode, excludes issuance from lifecycle writes, checks acknowledged revision CAS/exact patch readback and privately verifies retained supplied protected fields. Canonical private phase, original rights and simulated ITEM limits remain accurate.
